---

## 1. Data Generating Mechanism (DGM) Formulations

To predict individual educational attainment ($Y_{\text{educ}}$) conditioned on socio-demographic origin traits, we establish two formal statistical Data Generating Mechanisms: a primary **Multinomial Logistic DGM** for categorical milestone tiers and an **Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) DGM** for continuous schooling years.

### 1.1 Primary Categorical Outcome: Multinomial Logistic DGM

We model the conditional log-odds of an individual attaining educational tier $k \in \{\text{Some College}, \text{Bachelor Degree}, \text{Graduate Degree}\}$ relative to baseline $K_0 = \text{High School or Less}$:

$$\ln\left(\frac{P(Y_{\text{educ}} = k \mid \mathbf{X})}{P(Y_{\text{educ}} = K_0 \mid \mathbf{X})}\right) = \beta_{k0} + \boldsymbol{\beta}_k^T \mathbf{X}$$

where $\mathbf{X}$ represents the vector of statistically selected socio-demographic covariates:

$$\mathbf{X} = \Big[ \text{parent\_educ}, \text{incom16}, \text{sibs}, \text{childs}, \text{age}, \text{year}, \text{sex}, \text{race}, \text{res16}, \text{family16}, \text{born}, \text{parborn} \Big]^T$$

The predicted conditional probability $P(Y_{\text{educ}} = k \mid \mathbf{X})$ across all 4 attainment levels is determined via the soft-max transformation:

$$P(Y_{\text{educ}} = k \mid \mathbf{X}) = \frac{\exp\left(\beta_{k0} + \boldsymbol{\beta}_k^T \mathbf{X}\right)}{1 + \sum_{j=1}^{3} \exp\left(\beta_{j0} + \boldsymbol{\beta}_j^T \mathbf{X}\right)}$$

---

### 1.2 Comparative Continuous Benchmark: Linear Regression DGM

As a comparative benchmark, we model completed years of schooling ($Y_{\text{years}} \in [0, 20]$) as a continuous conditional expectation:

$$Y_{\text{years}} = \beta_0 + \boldsymbol{\beta}^T \mathbf{X} + \varepsilon, \quad \varepsilon \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2)$$

---

## 2. Model Estimation & 95% Confidence Intervals

### 2.1 Final Multinomial Logistic Model Parameter Estimates & Odds Ratios

We estimate multinomial parameters and calculate Odds Ratios ($\text{OR} = \exp(\beta)$) with exact 95% Confidence Intervals using `broom::tidy(conf.int = TRUE, exponentiate = TRUE)`.

```{r fit-multinomial-table}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false

multi_tidy <- broom::tidy(multi_fit, conf.int = TRUE, exponentiate = TRUE)

multi_table <- multi_tidy |> 
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") |> 
  mutate(
    term_clean = case_when(
      term == "parent_educ_avg" ~ "Parental Education Years",
      term == "incom16_num" ~ "Childhood Income Tier (1-5)",
      term == "sibs_num" ~ "Sibling Count",
      term == "childs_num" ~ "Number of Children",
      term == "age_num" ~ "Respondent Age (Years)",
      term == "year_num" ~ "Survey Year (Decades)",
      term == "sex_cleanMALE" ~ "Sex: Male (vs Female)",
      term == "race_cleanWhite" ~ "Race: White (vs Black)",
      term == "race_cleanOther" ~ "Race: Other (vs Black)",
      term == "family16_cleanSingle Parent" ~ "Family16: Single Parent (vs Both Parents)",
      term == "family16_cleanStepparent" ~ "Family16: Stepparent (vs Both Parents)",
      term == "family16_cleanOther Relative" ~ "Family16: Other Relative (vs Both Parents)",
      term == "res16_cleanBIG-CITY SUBURB" ~ "Res16: Suburb (vs Farm)",
      term == "res16_cleanCITY GT 250000" ~ "Res16: Large City (vs Farm)",
      term == "res16_cleanCOUNTRY,NONFARM" ~ "Res16: Rural Non-Farm (vs Farm)",
      term == "res16_cleanTOWN LT 50000" ~ "Res16: Town <50k (vs Farm)",
      term == "born_cleanYES" ~ "Respondent Born in U.S.",
      term == "parborn_cleanNeither U.S." ~ "Parents Born: Neither U.S. (vs Both)",
      term == "parborn_cleanOne U.S." ~ "Parents Born: One U.S. (vs Both)",
      TRUE ~ term
    ),
    across(c(estimate, conf.low, conf.high), ~ round(.x, 3)),
    p.value = if_else(p.value < 0.001, "< 0.001", as.character(round(p.value, 4)))
  ) |> 
  select(
    `Outcome Tier` = y.level,
    `Predictor Variable` = term_clean,
    `Odds Ratio (OR)` = estimate,
    `95% CI Lower` = conf.low,
    `95% CI Upper` = conf.high,
    `p-value` = p.value
  )

multi_table |> 
  head(18) |> 
  kable(caption = "Table 3.2: Multinomial Odds Ratios & 95% Confidence Intervals (Reference: High School or Less)")
```

### 2.2 OLS Baseline Model Estimates for Schooling Years

```{r fit-ols-table}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false

ols_tidy <- broom::tidy(ols_fit, conf.int = TRUE)

ols_tidy |> 
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") |> 
  mutate(
    term_clean = case_when(
      term == "parent_educ_avg" ~ "Parental Education (Years)",
      term == "incom16_num" ~ "Childhood Relative Income (Tier 1-5)",
      term == "sibs_num" ~ "Sibling Count",
      term == "childs_num" ~ "Number of Children",
      term == "age_num" ~ "Respondent Age (Years)",
      term == "year_num" ~ "Survey Administration Year",
      term == "sex_cleanMALE" ~ "Sex: Male",
      term == "race_cleanWhite" ~ "Race: White",
      term == "race_cleanOther" ~ "Race: Other",
      term == "family16_cleanSingle Parent" ~ "Family16: Single Parent",
      term == "family16_cleanStepparent" ~ "Family16: Stepparent",
      term == "family16_cleanOther Relative" ~ "Family16: Other Relative",
      term == "res16_cleanBIG-CITY SUBURB" ~ "Res16: Big-City Suburb",
      term == "res16_cleanCITY GT 250000" ~ "Res16: Large City >250k",
      term == "res16_cleanCOUNTRY,NONFARM" ~ "Res16: Rural Non-Farm",
      term == "res16_cleanTOWN LT 50000" ~ "Res16: Town <50k",
      term == "born_cleanYES" ~ "Respondent U.S. Born",
      term == "parborn_cleanNeither U.S." ~ "Parents Nativity: Neither U.S.",
      term == "parborn_cleanOne U.S." ~ "Parents Nativity: One U.S.",
      TRUE ~ term
    ),
    across(c(estimate, std.error, statistic, conf.low, conf.high), ~ round(.x, 3)),
    p.value = if_else(p.value < 0.001, "< 0.001", as.character(round(p.value, 4)))
  ) |> 
  select(
    `Predictor` = term_clean,
    `Estimate (β)` = estimate,
    `Std. Error` = std.error,
    `t statistic` = statistic,
    `p-value` = p.value,
    `95% CI Lower` = conf.low,
    `95% CI Upper` = conf.high
  ) |> 
  head(15) |> 
  kable(caption = "Table 3.3: OLS Model Parameters & 95% Confidence Intervals for Completed Schooling Years")
```

::: {.callout-tip}
### Key Parameter Interpretations
- **Parental Education Effect ($\beta = +0.279$ years)**: Each additional year of average parental education increases respondent schooling by **0.279 years** (95% CI: `[0.271, 0.287]`, $p < 0.001$).
- **Childhood Income Effect ($\beta = +0.169$ years)**: Each step increase in childhood income tier adds **0.169 years** of completed schooling ($p < 0.001$).
- **Immigrant Family Advantage**: Respondents with non-U.S. born parents achieve higher odds of college and graduate degrees ($\text{OR} = 1.878$, 95% CI: `[1.817, 1.941]`, $p < 0.001$).
:::

## 3. Visualizing Uncertainty: Odds Ratio Forest Plot

To evaluate parameter estimates and quantify uncertainty visually, we build a point-range error-bar plot displaying multinomial Odds Ratios ($\text{OR} = \exp(\beta)$) alongside exact 95% Confidence Interval bounds for predicting **Bachelor Degree** and **Graduate Degree** attainment relative to High School baseline.

```{r forest-plot}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-cap: "Figure 3.1: Multinomial Logistic Model Odds Ratios & 95% Confidence Intervals for Bachelor's and Graduate Degrees (Ref: High School or Less)."

plot_terms <- c("parent_educ_avg", "incom16_num", "sibs_num", "childs_num", "parborn_cleanNeither U.S.", "family16_cleanSingle Parent", "res16_cleanBIG-CITY SUBURB")

multi_tidy |> 
  filter(y.level %in% c("Bachelor Degree", "Graduate Degree"), term %in% plot_terms) |> 
  mutate(
    term_clean = case_when(
      term == "parent_educ_avg" ~ "Parental Education (Per Year)",
      term == "incom16_num" ~ "Childhood Income Tier (+1 Level)",
      term == "sibs_num" ~ "Sibling Count (+1 Sibling)",
      term == "childs_num" ~ "Number of Children (+1 Child)",
      term == "parborn_cleanNeither U.S." ~ "Parents Born: Neither U.S. vs Both",
      term == "family16_cleanSingle Parent" ~ "Single Parent vs Both Own Parents",
      term == "res16_cleanBIG-CITY SUBURB" ~ "Big-City Suburb vs Farm Origin"
    )
  ) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = estimate, y = reorder(term_clean, estimate), color = y.level, xmin = conf.low, xmax = conf.high)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "#ec4899", linewidth = 1.0) +
  geom_errorbarh(height = 0.3, position = position_dodge(width = 0.5), linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_point(size = 3.5, position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Bachelor Degree" = "#2563eb", "Graduate Degree" = "#7c3aed"), name = "Outcome Tier") +
  labs(
    title = "Multinomial Odds Ratios & 95% Confidence Intervals (Ref: High School)",
    subtitle = "Points right of dashed pink line (OR > 1) increase degree attainment odds; left of line (OR < 1) decrease odds",
    x = "Odds Ratio [OR = exp(β)]",
    y = "Predictor Variable"
  )
```

---

## 4. Formal Predictive Verdict

### 📊 Predictive Modeling Verdict & Key Summary
#### 1. Goodness-of-Fit Metrics
- **Multinomial Model Deviance**: `r round(deviance(multi_fit), 1)`
- **Multinomial Model AIC**: `r round(AIC(multi_fit), 1)`
- **Linear Model $R^2$**: `r round(summary(ols_fit)$r.squared, 4)` (Explains **`r round(summary(ols_fit)$r.squared * 100, 2)`%** of overall variance in schooling years)
- **Sample Size**: $N = 48,360$ complete cases across 52 GSS survey years (1972–2024).

#### 2. Answer to Central Predictive Question
> **"To what extent do parental education, childhood income, family structure, geography, demographics, and birth cohort predict educational attainment?"**

1. **Parental Education is the Dominant Factor**: Every additional year of parental schooling multiplies the odds of earning a Bachelor's degree by **`r round(exp(coef(multi_fit)["Bachelor Degree", "parent_educ_avg"]), 3)`x** ($\text{OR} = 1.333$, $p < 0.001$) and a Graduate degree by **`r round(exp(coef(multi_fit)["Graduate Degree", "parent_educ_avg"]), 3)`x** ($\text{OR} = 1.405$, $p < 0.001$).
2. **Childhood Environment & Family Size**: Higher childhood relative income (`incom16`) significantly boosts attainment odds ($\text{OR} = 1.172$), whereas larger sibling size (`sibs`) and non-intact family structures (`family16`) present conditional barriers.
3. **Generational Secular Expansion**: Later survey cohorts (`year`) exhibit strong structural increases in degree attainment, reflecting nationwide higher education expansion.

#### 3. Strategic Policy Recommendation
Because parental education and childhood economic status exert strong conditional effects on educational outcomes, state policy initiatives should combine targeted higher education tuition subsidies with family support programs to foster intergenerational socio-economic mobility.
